gaps.sentence: I ___ seeing that man somewhere before.
The ___ repairs were making the theatre impossible to run profitably.
She ___ the documents on the desk and left.
gaps.hint: past of the verb meaning 'put down' (takes an object)
gaps.explanation: 'Laid' is the past of 'lay' (put something down), which takes an object: she laid the documents.
'Besides' means in addition to; 'beside' means next to; 'except' means not including.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ me to post this letter.
gaps.hint: make somebody not forget: ___ somebody to do something
gaps.explanation: 'Remind somebody to do something' means to make someone remember; 'remember' is something you do yourself.

gaps.sentence: The committee ___ of eight members and two advisers.
gaps.explanation: 'Consist of' = be made up of; 'composes of' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: He ___ that he would be late.
gaps.hint: '___ that ...' without a listener as object
gaps.explanation: 'Say' is used with reported content ('say that ...') without a person object; 'tell' needs one (tell me that ...).

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.
